raw_response:
My land is about 10 mu — the same fields my father worked. I've been doing this my whole life. Quzhou is wheat-corn country. Everyone here plants wheat in the fall, harvests it in June, then turns around and puts corn in immediately on the same ground. That's what I'll do again this year. There's no reason to change what works.

For the wheat, I'll prepare the ground with rotary tillage after the corn comes off in October, then seed before the cold really sets in. I'll use the improved variety they sell at the township supply cooperative — I've used it the past few years and it does fine. I spread base fertilizer before planting: the diammonium phosphate and urea together, then I top-dress with more urea at jointing stage in spring. I irrigate before winter to help the seedlings establish, then again at jointing and heading. Four waterings total — I like to add one before freeze-up. Herbicide spray in winter, then a fungicide spray in spring when powdery mildew shows up. Harvest in June, maybe 450 jin a mu on a decent year.

Right after wheat harvest, I plant corn — no tilling, just direct seed into the stubble to save time and moisture. Hybrid seed, the kind郑单 or whatever the village cooperative stocks. Corn gets two good irrigations from me unless there's decent rain. I spray herbicide early, then check for corn borer in July and spray if I see it. Off the field by late September or early October.

That's my year. Simple. I'm 60 — I'm not trying anything new.
